permutationLabel: Base case — uncomplicated biliary colic, outpatient
summary: 38-year-old woman with four post-prandial episodes of RUQ pain over three months, pain-free now; normal observations, WBC, CRP and LFTs; ultrasound shows gallstones with a normal wall and a 4 mm CBD.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Episodes of right upper abdominal pain after meals
inputs.hpi: Four episodes over three months of severe right upper quadrant pain starting 30–60 minutes after fatty meals, lasting 2–4 hours, radiating to the right shoulder blade, with nausea. Completely well between episodes; the last episode was 5 days ago. No fever, no jaundice, no dark urine or pale stools. GP ultrasound shows gallstones. LMP 2 weeks ago.

exam.abdomen: Soft. Mild right upper quadrant tenderness on deep palpation only; Murphy's sign negative. No mass, no guarding.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Multiple mobile gallstones up to 12 mm. Gallbladder wall 2 mm, no pericholecystic fluid, sonographic Murphy's negative. CBD 4 mm. Liver and pancreas unremarkable.

inputs.socialHistory: Teacher. Non-smoker. Alcohol 2–3 units a week.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Biliary colic — symptomatic gallstones
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Biliary colic (symptomatic cholelithiasis). No features of cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis or pancreatitis. Normal LFTs, CBD 4 mm.

mustRankTopK.note: The index diagnosis. Quality: labelling biliary colic as cholecystitis over-treats but does not miss a dangerous condition.

emergencyLevel.note: Pain-free outpatient with normal observations and bloods: elective pathway. Over-triage to emergency is noise, not harm.

mustNotAlarm.note: The CBD measures 4 mm (normal). A "dilated CBD" alarm here is a false positive that drives MRCP/ERCP.
Afebrile, anicteric, pain-free: the HPI records "No fever, no jaundice". A Charcot/cholangitis alarm here comes from negated words.
mustNotAlarm.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts: replace the substring helpers exam()/hasSx()/hasRadResult() and hasFever (which matches "temp" and "afebrile") with a negation-aware matcher (NegEx-style: no/not/without/denies/negative/absent within ~5 tokens) and read fever from the temperature vital (≥38 °C), not from text.

redFlags.note: Safety-netting: fever, jaundice or persistent pain should prompt urgent return.

recommended.note: ASGE 2019 risk stratification for CBD stones (here: low risk) before cholecystectomy.

mustInclude.note: NICE CG188: offer laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallbladder stones.

mustExclude.note: No infection: antibiotics for uncomplicated biliary colic are not indicated (stewardship).
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Assessment panel shows the cholecystitis protocol (PANE top) with IV co-amoxiclav/pip-tazo; the Murphy's-sign prompt (fired by "Murphy's sign negative") adds IV co-amoxiclav.
mustExclude.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts: replace the substring helpers exam()/hasSx()/hasRadResult() and hasFever (which matches "temp" and "afebrile") with a negation-aware matcher (NegEx-style: no/not/without/denies/negative/absent within ~5 tokens) and read fever from the temperature vital (≥38 °C), not from text.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
mustExclude.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts SURGICAL PATHWAY CASCADE: gate hasAppendicitisIndication/hasGallstoneIndication on the working diagnosis or assessment (as the Alvarado block already does with assessmentHasAppend) and on positive, non-negated findings — not on any "guarding", "gallbladder wall" or "gallstone" substring.

guideline.name: NICE CG188 — Gallstone disease: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Asymptomatic gallbladder stones in a normal gallbladder and biliary tree: reassure, no treatment; symptomatic gallbladder stones: offer laparoscopic cholecystectomy; LFTs and ultrasound for suspected gallstone disease
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG188, October 2014.

guideline.name: ASGE guideline on the role of endoscopy in the evaluation and management of choledocholithiasis
guideline.section: Risk strata. High: CBD stone on US/cross-sectional imaging, or total bilirubin >4 mg/dL with dilated CBD, or ascending cholangitis → ERCP. Intermediate: abnormal liver tests, age >55, or dilated CBD → EUS/MRCP or intra-operative cholangiography/laparoscopic US. Low: none → cholecystectomy without further CBD evaluation
guideline.citation: Buxbaum JL, Abbas Fehmi SM, Sultan S, et al. Gastrointest Endosc. 2019;89:1075–1105.e15.

rationale: Base case for the gallstone spectrum: a pain-free outpatient with symptomatic gallstones and no complication. Tests that the engines name biliary colic (PANE has no biliary-colic node), do not escalate or alarm, do not add antibiotics, and offer elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The exam text contains a negated sign ("Murphy's sign negative") to probe negation handling.
